summary: A note on the cost of network software, using the survey mechanisms that hosts use to see who is up as an example of wasted overhead. MIT-DMCG and UCLA-NMC agreed on a standard format for host survey data and would make it available, so others need not poll. The title is a quote from complaints.

eli5.summary: Lots of computers keep asking others are you awake, which costs effort. Instead, a few will ask and share the answer.

questions: why surveying arpanet hosts is costly
subtitle: A standard host status service to reduce network polling overhead

tldr.problem: Many sites were running independent host survey mechanisms to see which hosts were up, creating significant network overhead and wasted computation that was not chargeable to any user.
tldr.mechanism: MIT-DMCG and UCLA-NMC agreed on a standard format for host survey data and made it available at a standard socket. Other sites would query the official surveyors periodically rather than polling hosts themselves.
tldr.outcome: Eliminating redundant polling would reduce network noise and the cost of the network control protocol.

today: This proposal established the principle of centralized status monitoring for networks. Modern network monitoring services and status dashboards follow the same pattern of collecting information at a few points and distributing it rather than having every client poll every server.

sections.title: The Cost of Host Surveys
sections.content: As network use became more common, sites began measuring the cost of their network software and network usage. They discovered that a significant amount of network overhead came from host surveys—mechanisms that many sites built independently to check 'who's up' on the network. Several systems found that this survey activity alone accounted for a large portion of their overhead and could not be charged to any specific user.
sections.eli5: Every computer on the network kept asking other computers if they were awake, wasting a lot of time and effort.

sections.title: Standard Host Survey Data
sections.content: In response to this problem, MIT-DMCG and UCLA-NMC, both of which had been doing host surveys for some time, agreed upon a standard format for host survey data and made it available to the network community at a standard socket number. A third site joined this effort, forming a group of Official Surveyors that would perform the surveys on behalf of the entire network.
sections.eli5: Three big computer sites agreed to ask if other computers were awake, and everyone else could just ask them instead of asking directly.

sections.title: Reducing Network Noise
sections.content: The goal was for all other sites to stop surveying hosts independently and instead get host status data from one of the Official Surveyors, either prompted by a user's request or on a periodic basis. The standard format for the data was designed to be concise and both human-readable and machine-readable, making it efficient to transmit and process. This approach would help eliminate much of the network traffic that contributed to the 'noise factor' on ARPANET.
sections.eli5: By having just a few central check points instead of everyone asking, the whole network uses less effort.

sections.title: Network Cost Awareness
sections.content: Beyond the standardized survey service, the RFC also urged all sites to become more aware of the cost of network traffic and to avoid making repeated interactions with a given host without some expressed consent, such as an account number or some specific experiment justification. This awareness of cost and efficiency became important as network use grew.
sections.eli5: Everyone should think about how much effort they are using on the network and ask permission before using someone else's computer a lot.
